successors.name: Magadha
successors.text: all of Anga: 'Anga became part of the Magadhi empire, and Campa became the seat of a Magadhi viceroy'

ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Anga, easternmost of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Champa. The page lists Anga among the 'sixteen great nations' of the Anguttara Nikaya ('Anga is the easternmost, south of Vajji and east of Magadha') and dates Dadhivahana's reign to the 6th century BCE; -600 is the Mahajanapada convention…
Early 6th century BCE: Anga under Dadhivahana overruns Magadha.
543 BCE: Bimbisara takes the Magadhan throne and Magadha is Anga's no longer.

c. 530 BCE: Bimbisara of Magadha kills Brahmadatta and annexes Anga; Champa becomes a viceroy's seat. 'Bimbisara Srenika avenged his father's defeat against Anga by defeating and killing the Angeya king Brahmadatta' in the middle of the 6th century BCE, 'after which Anga became part of the Magadhi empire, and Campa…

wars.name: Anga-Magadha wars
wars.outcome: Anga under Dadhivahana conquered Magadha and Brahmadatta defeated Bimbisara's father; Bimbisara then defeated and killed Brahmadatta and annexed Anga (c.

wars.name: Kalinga's attack on Anga
wars.outcome: 'the state of Kalinga attacked Anga and took Dadhivahana captive'; Udayana 'was able to defeat Kalinga and restore Dadhivahana on the Angeya throne'.

certainty.note: No frontier is recorded; the shape is the Champa country between the Champa river and the Rajmahal hills.
